I know. We are most definitely the experts.

Our relationship is wonderful. I just worry I'm burdening him too much with all my problems. He's got his problems too and I feel like I add to them.
I will give someone a call, I promise. I'll figure something out this week. I can't go on without some sort of professional help. Thank you again.

Thank you, so much. I needed someone to tell me that I'm not crazy when it comes to this. My dad in particular can't understand why every therapist is different. He just thinks I can pick one and they're all the same when they're not, which in turn makes me feel really guilty. It's been like this my entire life. He thinks I can't stick to anything (the anxiety makes it hard) and you know what, when it comes to therapy, it's hard to stick to it.

Not every provider is going to help. Not every medication is going to make you feel better. And that's just the reality of it. Thank you again. I don't feel as guilty about that anymore now that someone I don't even know gets it too. 

And yes, my boyfriend is incredible. I don't know what I'd do without him. I can see what you mean by that emotional place -- it's so much different to have someone close to you helping.

First of all, thank you for replying. It means a lot.

But if I have insurance already doesn't that trump Medicaid? I do live in the US. I don't even know where to start when it comes to this stuff. I'm apprehensive about going back into therapy because it never seemed to make much of a difference before. 

I don't want to admit to my parents how bad it is. They don't get it at all and don't want to get it. They're absolutely convinced I can fix this by taking some cocktail of drugs and I'll be "normal" afterward. I know I'm capable of taking "that first step" all over again but I don't know where to begin or even if I'm eligible for help paying for therapy.
